newsitem.title: UK: Capital says merger not anti-competitive.
newsitem.headline: Capital says merger not anti-competitive.

text.p: Britain's Capital Radio Plc said on Thursday its planned 64.7 million stg merger with Virgin Radio has no competitive implications.

The comments came after Nigel Griffiths, minister for competition and consumer affairs, announced earlier today the deal would be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission due to concern about competition in London's radio advertising market.
"We continue to believe that the proposed deal has no competitive implications," said Capital in a statement.

The development of Capital and Virgin as distinct radio brands is in the "best interests of listeners and advertisers as it will provide the opportunity to challenge BBC Radio in the new digital age," said the group in a statement.
If the deal is allowed to go-ahead it would give Capital a total of three licenses in London - Capital FM, Capital Gold (AM) and Virgin FM - in addition to one national AM licence.
Capital Radio shares closed 16p lower at 490p.
